title: Pulling back a decision tree
statement: Let $m,n$ be natural numbers, let $\alpha$ be a type, and let $e:[m]\hookrightarrow[n]$ be an embedding. For finite coordinate sets $S\subseteq[m]$ and $T\subseteq[n]$ such that $i\in S$ exactly when $e(i)\in T$, every binary decision tree on $[n]$ with available coordinates $T$ induces a binary decision tree on $[m]$ with available coordinates $S$: a query at a coordinate in the image of $e$ becomes the query at its unique preimage, while a query outside that image is discarded and the zero branch is retained; leaves retain their values.
